# Tagged sample lines for lint-suppression-added, one per line:
#   <tag> TAB <file name> TAB <sample>
# `+` the rule fires on a fragment holding the sample, `-` it stays silent; `r`
# it fires and every hit carries a reason, `b` it fires and none does; `n+` and
# `n-` a whole change (file name `old>new` for a rename, sample `before@@after`)
# does or does not add a marker once removals are netted. The
# file name decides the file type; `\n` in a sample is a line break. A fragment
# has no file around it, so samples that need a section carry their header.
#
# Two classifiers read this file and must agree: the Rust one in
# src/rules/lint_suppression_added.rs (a unit test) and the transcript scanner
# tools/suppression-rate.py (--self-test, run by tests/suppression_rate.rs).
